title: DNP3 application fragment
description: One DNP3 application fragment (IEEE 1815): a request, a response or an unsolicited response, carried as the JSON payload of a ProtocolMessage on the <topic_base>/out/dnp3-raw topic. Open to new fields: a field not listed here is allowed and should not be relied on until it is listed. A listed field must have its type and bound, and is null only where stated. `schema` is raised only for a change a consumer must handle. Integers that IEEE 1815 carries as octets or unsigned integers, range fields included, are bounded to their wire width, and analog values to the range of a double. A parser also checks what this schema cannot: a range's start is not above its stop, a number is not NaN, and a pattern matches the whole string. The `format` keywords on the IP fields are checked only by a validator with format assertion turned on.

source_address.description: Link-layer source address of the station that sent the fragment.

function_code.description: Application function code, as on the wire. 129 RESPONSE, 130 UNSOLICITED_RESPONSE and 131 AUTHENTICATE_RESP come from an outstation; every other defined code comes from a master.

prm.description: Link-layer primary-message (PRM) bit of the frames that carried the fragment. Application data travels in primary frames, so conforming traffic has 1.

direction.description: request: sent by the master. response: sent by the outstation, including an unsolicited response.

unsolicited.description: The application control UNS bit as on the wire. A conforming outstation sets it on every unsolicited response (function code 130), and a conforming master sets it on the CONFIRM of one.

iin.description: Internal indications of a response: the names of the bits set in IIN1 and IIN2. An empty list means no bit is set. Required on a response unless apdu_rejected is present; never present on a request.

source_ip.description: IP address of the sender. Absent when the fragment did not travel over IP or the producer withholds it.

source_port.description: TCP or UDP port of the sender.

destination_port.description: TCP or UDP port of the receiver.

objects.description: One entry per object header, in wire order. A 2048-octet fragment holds at most 682.

points.description: Every point the fragment carries, status and command objects alike, in wire order. A 2048-octet fragment holds at most 16,328.

apdu_rejected.description: Present when the fragment's object data cannot be trusted, with the reason: malformed (it could not be decoded to its end), point_count (an object header's range or count disagrees with the objects that follow) or too_large (it holds more object headers or points than this schema allows). A rejected fragment reports no objects and no points.

analog_value.description: Any value a 16- or 32-bit integer, single- or double-precision variation can carry: the range of a double.

iin_bit.description: An internal indication bit by its IEEE 1815 name (Table 4-3 and 4.5), IIN1.0 (broadcast) through IIN2.7 (reserved_1), in that order.

object_header.description: One object header. The qualifier's low nibble, the range specifier code (IEEE 1815 Table 4-5), decides the range fields and their width: codes 0 and 3 carry one-octet start and stop, 1 and 4 two-octet, 2 and 5 four-octet (indices for 0 to 2, virtual addresses for 3 to 5); codes 7 and 11 carry a one-octet count, 8 two-octet, 9 four-octet; every other code carries none. start is not above stop, which a parser checks.

variation.description: 0 asks for any variation, in a read.

qualifier.description: The qualifier octet: object prefix code in bits 4 to 6, range specifier code in bits 0 to 3.

data.description: The object octets after the header, index or size prefixes included, in lowercase hex. Present when octets follow a header of a group whose objects are not points (time and date, files, device attributes and the like), so a write keeps what it sets. Never on a header of a point group: its objects are in points.

point.description: One point. type is the point type, set by the group; group and variation say which object carried it (static, event, frozen, command). index is the point index on the wire. Fields a group does not carry are absent. A group 12 variation 2 point is a pattern control block applied to one output its pattern mask (group 12 variation 3) selects.

command.description: true for a control object: a CROB (group 12) or an analog output block (group 41), in a request or echoed in a response.

value.description: The point's value, typed by point type. Null only for an analog type whose floating-point value is not finite, with non_finite saying which.

non_finite.description: Present exactly when value is null: the non-finite floating-point value on the wire.

flags.description: The flag octet as on the wire, for a variation that carries one. For binary types it includes the state bits. Absent for a variation without flags, which IEEE 1815 defines as online.

time.description: DNP3 time: milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z on the outstation's clock. A relative-time object is resolved against its common time of occurrence.

op_type.description: CROB: control code bits 0 to 3. 0 NUL, 1 PULSE_ON, 2 PULSE_OFF, 3 LATCH_ON, 4 LATCH_OFF.

trip_close.description: CROB: control code bits 6 and 7, the trip-close code. 0 NUL, 1 CLOSE, 2 TRIP, 3 RESERVED.

queue.description: CROB: control code bit 4, obsolete and required to be clear.

count.description: CROB: how many times to repeat the operation.

status.description: Control status code as on the wire (0 SUCCESS), on a CROB, an analog output block, and their command events (groups 13 and 43).
